title: P0: Dedicated customer OOM cascade from stale session-shard retention + allocator slab fragmentation
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Summary: A major Dedicated customer experienced repeated GPU OOM cascades during high-concurrency inference runs. Initial mitigation (restarts) reduced immediate churn but did not prevent recurrence. Investigation points to long-lived session-shard objects that retained KV-cache handles across model switches combined with a slab allocator fragmentation pattern that prevented reuse of freed tensor arenas, causing steady native memory growth and eventual GPU OOMs under burst traffic. A runtime patch is required to add eager shard eviction and a slab coalescer to reclaim fragmented arenas.

reproduction_steps:
1) Deploy inference workload that opens many concurrent sessions and frequently switches model variants (A->B->A).
2) Enable prefix caching and KV handle pinning (replicate customer routing rules).
3) Run sustained high concurrency (50-200 reqs/s per node) with sequence lengths > 2k tokens.
4) Observe native memory rise in heap profiles and occasional CUDA OOMs when fragmentation prevents contiguous allocations.
5) Use heap and arena dumps to confirm stranded tensor arenas and non-zero refcounts on session-shard handles.
mitigation_actions_taken:
- Short-term: node restart policy and increased swap buffer for Dedicated pool (applied 2026-03-08).
- Medium-term: activated aggressive session eviction for the affected customer (TTL reduced from 60m -> 5m).
- Long-term: implemented allocator coalescing and explicit shard drop on model version change (PR links below).
root_cause: Two interacting issues: 1) Session-shard objects retained KV-cache handles across rapid model variant switches, preventing proper eviction of associated tensor arenas. 2) Our slab allocator could not coalesce adjacent free slabs under certain allocation/free patterns caused by large transient KV buffers, producing fragmentation that required contiguous memory for GPU allocations. Together these produced a slow native memory leak and sudden contiguous allocation failures (GPU OOM) during bursts.
resolution_summary: Created runtime patch that: (a) tracks session-shard liveness and drops stale KV handles after configurable inactivity; (b) implements a slab coalescer that merges adjacent free slabs on deallocation and triggers arena compaction when fragmentation crosses threshold; (c) adds telemetry counters for shard retention and fragmentation percentage. Deployed to canary and observed no regressions under stress tests. Preparing gradual rollout to Dedicated and then Hosted.
rollout_plan:
1) Canary: runtime-1.26 canary cluster (10% Dedicated traffic) - already running since 2026-03-11.
2) Monitor for 72h with stress harness and customer traffic.
3) If stable, promote to remaining Dedicated pools in 2 waves (50% then 100%) over 48h.
4) Apply to Private on-request with patch artifact and upgrade notes.
5) Post-mortem and follow-up tasks scheduled after full rollout.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for shard TTL and handle lifecycle.
- Integration test simulating model switches and KV handle churn.
- Stress test: sustained high concurrency with variable seq lengths on canary nodes.
- Heap/arena assertion: fragmentation % must drop below 20% under churn.
- Nightly regression: run differential perf compare vs runtime-1.25 to validate no latency regressions.
follow_ups: Add automatic fragmentation alert (console) tied to per-route dashboards
Investigate opportunistic page compaction for private/on-prem kernels
Add regression unit to CI that runs model-switch stress case nightly
